user.title: Heat Ledger
user.description:
Splits the heat of your heating between rooms and hot water. Three short steps follow, in the order the heat flows: heat source, pumps, room heating. Everything can be added or changed later on the integration page.

There is no back button in these steps: if something went wrong, close the dialog and start again.

source.title: Heat source
source.description: Where does the heat come from? A meter of your heating: gas meter, oil consumption, heat meter or the heat output of a heat pump. A gas source of the Energy dashboard is preselected. More sources (fireplace, immersion heater) can be added later.

data_description.name: What you call the source, e.g. oil burner, gas boiler, heat pump. Empty: the name of the meter.
data_description.entity_id: A meter reading that only increases, e.g. in kWh, m³ or L.
data_description.quantity: Heat: already converted, e.g. a heat meter or the heat output a heat pump reports. Energy input: gas, oil or electricity before the boiler or heater turns it into heat; the next step asks for the factor. For a heat pump, always choose its heat output, not its electricity.

factor.title: Conversion to heat
factor.description:
How many kWh of heat does 1 {unit} of {name} give?

- **Gas in m³:** about 9 to 10. Calorific value × z-number × boiler efficiency; calorific value and z-number are on the gas bill.
- **Heating oil in litres:** about 9. A litre of heating oil holds about 10 kWh, the boiler turns about 90 % of it into heat.
- **Gas, oil or pellets in kWh:** about 0.9, the efficiency of the boiler.
- **Burner run time in hours:** the output of the burner in kW, only for a burner without modulation.
- **Electricity of an immersion heater:** 1.
- **Electricity of a heat pump:** not recommended, its efficiency changes a lot with the outdoor temperature. Use the heat output the heat pump reports instead, as a source that counts heat: close this dialog and start again. Only if there is none: about 3.

data_description.factor: kWh of heat per unit of the reading.

pumps.title: Pumps
pumps.description:
The pumps tell when heat flows to the rooms or into the hot water. Both fields are optional, but make the split much more accurate.

**No binary sensor for a pump?** If it is plugged into a smart plug or switch that measures power (e.g. a Shelly), create a **Threshold** helper on that power (on above about 5 W): Settings → Devices & services → Helpers. If your boiler's integration reports the pump state, use that.

data_description.circuit_pump: On while the pump runs that moves the water through radiators or underfloor heating. Without it, a room heating counts whenever its thermostat asks for heat, even while the boiler only heats water.
data_description.hot_water_pump: On while the hot water tank is being heated: its charging pump, or the hot water status of the boiler (also for a combi boiler). Not the circulation pump that keeps hot water moving to the taps. Without it, the heat for hot water is split between the rooms.

thermostats.title: Room heating
thermostats.description:
Choose the thermostats of your radiators or underfloor heating, also room controllers with actuators: each one becomes a room heating with its own heat counter. Many thermostats (Tado, for example) carry the name of their room, so you may see room names here. If a thermostat reports its heating demand in %, that is used.

Sizes, circuits and more room heating can be added later on the integration page. Home Assistant then asks for the area of each new device; it is already filled in where the thermostat or pump has one.

data_description.thermostats: Climate entities, one per room or radiator.

init.title: Heating system
init.description: Sources, circuits and consumers are edited on the integration page, each through its own entry.

data_description.loss_kw: Heat lost all the time by a storage tank and pipes, in kW. It is taken off before the split and shows as "Untracked" in the Energy dashboard. Leave empty if unknown: the losses then go to the consumers as well.

circuit.title: Heating circuit
circuit.description:
Room heating behind one pump, e.g. the radiators or the underfloor heating. Without a running pump, none of it gets heat. The circuit gets a heat counter of its own, in the Energy dashboard the upstream device of its room heating. Which room heating belongs to it is set on the room heating.

**No binary sensor for the pump?** If it is plugged into a smart plug or switch that measures power (e.g. a Shelly), create a **Threshold** helper on that power (on above about 5 W): Settings → Devices & services → Helpers.

data_description.name: For example radiators, underfloor heating or the floor.
data_description.pump_entity_id: On while the circuit pump runs. Without it, the circuit only groups its room heating and counts as always running.

error.wrong_domain: This type of entity is not supported here.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Saved. The plant is reloaded with the change.

radiator.title: Room heating
radiator.description: A radiator or an underfloor heating with its own heat counter. Gets a share of the heat by its size and demand. Home Assistant then asks for the area; if the thermostat has one, it is already filled in.

data_description.name: Empty: the name of the thermostat or demand.
data_description.circuit: Without a circuit, the room heating is always supplied.
data_description.demand_entity_id: Thermostat, heating demand or valve position in %, or an on/off actuator. Without one, it counts as always heating.

data_description.demand_type: Only for a demand sensor in %.
data_description.size_type: By default, all room heating counts as equal.
data_description.size_value: Floor area in m² or nominal power in W, as chosen above.
data_description.meter_entity_id: Measures the heat of this room heating. Replaces the estimate.

demand_suggestion.title: Demand in %
demand_suggestion.description: {sensor} reports the heating demand of {climate} in percent. That is more accurate than heating on/off.

data_description.use_suggestion: Off: use heating on/off of the thermostat.

hot_water.title: Hot water
hot_water.description:
Gets heat while the hot water tank is being heated.

**No binary sensor for the pump?** If it is plugged into a smart plug or switch that measures power (e.g. a Shelly), create a **Threshold** helper on that power (on above about 5 W): Settings → Devices & services → Helpers. If your boiler's integration reports the hot water status, use that.

data_description.name: For example hot water or the storage tank.
data_description.demand_entity_id: On while the tank is being heated: its charging pump, or the hot water status of the boiler (also for a combi boiler). Not the circulation pump. Not needed if a heat meter measures the heat.

data_description.charging_power_kw: Heat while the pump runs, in kW. Default: 10 kW.
data_description.meter_entity_id: Measures the heat for hot water. Replaces the estimate.
